matched.note: Same defect: policy.go's policyBase() trusts the working-tree acdsl/policy.json's BaseRef field, so a branch committing base_ref=its-own-branch-name makes isBoundary false and CheckPolicy short-circuits with zero diagnostics. Confirmed in code: policyBase (internal/acdsl/policy.go:190-216) sets candidates=[]string{policy.BaseRef} when non-empty and returns branch != baseName with no verification the value came from a trusted source.

Same underlying mechanism as GV3-001 (isBoundary computed from attacker-controlled BaseRef causes CheckPolicy to return nil before diffing) — SP-001 covers both the security and correctness framing of this one defect.

Same defect family: golden GV3-153 documents that no plan in the v1-2-1 set approves the new subagent-spill-enforcement mechanism in read-gate.sh, and explicitly notes it 'pairs with the equally-undocumented new cmd/hooks/skill-invoke-gate.sh'. SP-002 names skill-invoke-gate.sh as the file but the same root cause (undocumented hook-behavior change, no plan reference) applies verbatim; verified plans/v1-2-1/2026-08-26-railroad-review-observability-wip-5158764 never mentions skill-invoke-gate.sh in its design doc (only in a runbook trace).

Same code change: settings/claude_code/settings.json's removal of the four Edit(acdsl/**)/Write(acdsl/**) ask entries (verified via git diff at line ~105). Golden frames the consequence as a security gap for non-adopting repos; SP-003 frames the same removal as undocumented against the acdsl-policy-modes plan (verified: plans/v1-2-1/2026-08-26-acdsl-policy-modes-done-a7cd7bf/design/raw.md scopes the settings.json change to hook registration only and explicitly excludes settings emission from scope) — same root defect (the removal shipped without an accounted-for compensating control), different angle.

falsePositives.reason: Out of range: the claimed test failure (TestDistShipsReachCoveredSliceWithBinaries) is caused by local working-tree corruption, not the reviewed diff. Verified: `git status --short acdsl/` shows acdsl/policy.json, acdsl/registry.json, acdsl/rules.acdsl as modified/dirty against HEAD in the arm-wt checkout; `git show HEAD:acdsl/registry.json` proves every committed entry still uses the 3-element go-run argv shape (e.g. gofmt -> ["go","run","./cmd/acdsl/verifiers/gofmtwrap"]) that writeDistRegistry correctly rewrites, while the dirty working copy has already been overwritten with 1-element prebuilt-path entries (e.g. ["bin/verifiers/gofmt"]) that dist_test.go's repoRoot="../.." reads from disk. So the failure this candidate describes is a harness/environment artifact exactly as SP-004 itself states, not a defect in the reviewed commits — SP-004 does not allege an in-range code defect (empty fix field), so it cannot be uncataloged either.
